title: Platform registry
description: registry/registry.json: the single source of truth for the platform (domain, hosting, gateway, sign-in) and every application on it. The portal tiles, firebase.json rewrites and gateway routes are all rendered from this file. The published copy at https://eisensoftware.com/registry.json is this object plus a generatedAt timestamp, with each app's `repo` block removed (private repository names and local paths); `platform.auth` and each app's `access` are public and stay in it. Each app's `deployment` block is patched by CI when an app repo reports a deploy. Rules JSON Schema cannot express (unique ids, paths and group ids; every access group declared in platform.auth.groups) are enforced by scripts/validate-registry.mjs.

then.description: An app with `access` needs the platform's sign-in (platform.auth).

generatedAt.description: Only present in the published copy.

site.description: Firebase Hosting site id that serves the apex domain.

enabled.description: When true, render-firebase emits the gateway rewrite.

service.description: Cloud Run service id of the gateway.

auth.description: Platform sign-in (docs/runbooks/platform-auth.md). Identity is Firebase Authentication in `projectId`; a person's groups are the custom claim `groups` (an array of group ids), written only by scripts/grant-groups.mjs. Apps with an `access` block are served through the gateway door while `enabled` and platform.gateway.enabled are both true.

enabled.description: When true (and the gateway is enabled), render-firebase rewrites every app with `access` to the gateway service: the door. When false, those apps are routed to their own service, unguarded.

projectId.description: Firebase / GCP project that issues the ID tokens (token `aud`; `iss` is https://securetoken.google.com/<projectId>).

sessionHours.description: Lifetime of a door session (the sealed `__session` cookie) in hours. A group removed from a person keeps working in a session sealed before the removal until it expires.

groups.description: The group profiles. Ids are unique (enforced by scripts/validate-registry.mjs); apps[].access.groups may name only these ids.

apps.description: One entry per application. ids and paths are unique across the array (enforced by scripts/validate-registry.mjs).

then.description: The gateway door forwards to a Cloud Run service, so an app with `access` must be web.kind cloud-run.

id.description: Slug, unique across apps. `registry`, `health` and `auth` are reserved: they would shadow the gateway's <prefix>/registry, <prefix>/health and <prefix>/auth/* routes.

description.description: One sentence shown on the tile.

icon.description: An emoji or short glyph shown on the tile.

status.description: live and beta render as tiles; planned renders dimmed; hidden is not rendered.

path.description: Path prefix on the platform domain, unique across apps.

ready.description: true once the app serves correctly under `path` through the Hosting rewrite. Until then tiles link to web.url.

service.description: Cloud Run service id (kind = cloud-run). Used for the Hosting rewrite.

baseUrl.description: Upstream base the gateway forwards /api/<id>/* to.

docs.description: Path or URL of the API description (OpenAPI).

access.description: Who may enter. Present = the app is served only through the gateway door (Hosting rewrites <path>{,/**} to the gateway while platform.auth.enabled and platform.gateway.enabled): sign-in required, and the person's `groups` claim must share a group with `groups`. Absent = public. Requires platform.auth and web.kind cloud-run.

groups.description: Group ids declared in platform.auth.groups; a person in any one of them passes. [] = any signed-in person.

localPath.description: Where the checkout lives on Jordan's machine (informational).

deployment.description: Written by CI only: .github/workflows/sync-deployments.yml (pulls each app's health JSON every 30 min) and .github/workflows/register-deployment.yml (repository_dispatch `app-deployed`, optional and faster).

group.description: A group profile: the value of the `groups` claim is a list of these ids; name, emblem and description are what people see.

id.description: Slug stored in the `groups` custom claim; unique across groups.

emblem.description: An emoji or short glyph (at most 8 characters, counted as Unicode code points).
